Folks —

Looping in quick tech details on why forwarded invites sometimes "float": when the ICS is created without a TZID property for the DTSTART/DTEND or if the client strips the VTIMEZONE block on forward, some calendars interpret the event as floating (no timezone anchor) and render it in the recipient’s local time without applying DST offsets consistently. In practice the common culprits are:

- A generated .ics that sets DTSTART as a local time without TZID
- Missing VTIMEZONE blocks in the ICS payload
- Google Calendar UI forwarding that rewrites the invite and loses the VTIMEZONE

Short-term fixes I recommend we try immediately:
1) Reissue the invite with an explicit TZID (Europe/London) and include a full VTIMEZONE block.
2) Add an explicit UTC anchor in the description (e.g., "Event time: 2027-05-12 15:00 UTC / 16:00 BST / 11:00 ET").
3) If the customer forwards to an Exchange/Outlook/Safari calendar, ask them to add the event from the confirmation email rather than forwarding the ICS.

I’ve attached a corrected stub I can send from our calendar service that sets TZID correctly. If you want, I can push it out as a new invite and mark the old as canceled.

Attachment: invite-anchored.ics (text/calendar)

—Jonas
